summary.headline: Synergy Green H1 FY27 PBDIT margin fell to 8.9% from 15.6% on input-cost inflation, while management reaffirmed 33% FY27 revenue growth and ~100 bp margin expansion.
summary.overview: Management said H1 FY27 production rose 25.8% YoY and revenue rose 20.2%, but PBDIT margin compressed to 8.9% (Q2 at 10.2% vs 15.7% a year earlier) due to commodity and consumable inflation, logistics costs and under-absorbed ramp-up costs. Export shipments were delayed by ship and logistics constraints, building inventory that is carried at cost and not in revenue. Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth of 33% (about Rs 500 crore), exports up over 50% to about 30% of revenue, and FY27 margin up about 100 bp, implying 17-18% H2 EBITDA margin. Demand was described as strong, mainly from US wind OEMs, with greenfield expansion deferred until current capacity is stabilised.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 159.76 crore in H1 FY26 (as stated on call)

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 1.3 crore to Rs 3 crore (management cited both figures)

segments.name: Wind castings (domestic and export)
segments.commentary: Wind castings are about 70% of the portfolio; wind domestic revenue grew strongly in H1 YoY. OEM exports were in line with last year, with growth expected in H2.

segments.name: Gearbox castings
segments.commentary: Gearbox castings for wind are about 15% of the portfolio, with Flender and ZF among customers.

segments.name: Non-wind (cone crushers, coal pulverisers, mining, pumps)
segments.commentary: Remaining portion of the portfolio. Management is de-prioritising non-wind to focus capacity on wind, citing complexity and margin focus; machine-tool demand (e.g. Mahindra) could not be served.

segments.name: Machine shop
segments.commentary: Utilisation at 45-50% of machining capacity (20,000 tpa in-house); seven or eight products developed; management expects a good contribution in about 5-6 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 33% reaffirmed; management says the top line is not a constraint and Rs 500 crore turnover is achievable.
Exports expected to grow over 50% in FY27 and contribute about 30% of revenue (about 25% last year).
FY27 PBDIT/EBITDA margin expected to rise about 100 bp YoY; implies about 17-18% EBITDA margin in H2 versus 8.9% in H1.
Management guides EBITDA growth of about 50% and cash profit growth above 50% for FY27, with most of it in H2; net profit targeted to turn positive by year-end (described as roughly break-even).
Capacity utilisation expected at about 75% in H1, about 85% in H2, and about 80% for FY27 on 45,000 tpa.
Revenue potential from current 45,000 tpa capacity revised to Rs 600-650 crore (previously Rs 550-600 crore), citing inflation pass-through.
Management expects FY28 growth of about 25-30% and aims for about 25% CAGR; greenfield expansion is planned for FY29 and further debottlenecking of about 10-15% capacity is being explored.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 45,000 tpa foundry (raised from 30,000 tpa in March 2026), plus about 20,000 tpa in-house machining and surface treatment; 10 MW captive solar.
Utilisation about 75% in H1 FY27, targeted at about 85% in H2 and about 80% for FY27.
Greenfield project needs about 15-18 months to build; to be phased, with stabilisation of current capacity first (about two quarters). Suzlon has approached the company to localise components.
Management said a further 10-15% capacity addition on the existing 45,000 tpa is being evaluated; no greenfield capex amount was given.
Captive solar and wind open-access power covers about 60% of electricity needs; captive solar yields about Rs 7-8/unit savings versus grid.
demand_pricing: Management reports no demand slowdown; US wind OEMs (Vestas, Nordex, and newer entrants) describe orders as open-book, with customers asking for more capacity. Demand is said to exceed 60,000 tpa against 45,000 tpa capacity.

Pricing: annual contracts are fixed for 12 months, with quarterly indexation on pig iron, CRC and furan. Pass-through is about 8-10% of cost increase, with a one-quarter lag; Q3 weighted average price increase about 5%. Management notes 100-150 bp margin impact in high-inflation periods.
Cost pressures: furan resin up 50%+ in Q1; commodities rising in Q2; logistics costs roughly threefold; Maharashtra power tariff up over 20% from April.
Export logistics: ODC shipments are constrained by ship availability; customers pay about 50-60% of component cost in freight for US shipments; October shipments reportedly 60-70% moving.

Competition: management is not concerned about a competitor's planned capacity addition (said to be about 3x), arguing Indian demand exceeds supply and OEMs will not single-source. Chinese castings face US tariffs, favouring Indian suppliers; RMB appreciation is expected to narrow the cost gap.

Customer base: works with 6 of the top 15 global wind OEMs (Vestas, Envision, Siemens Gamesa, Nordex, Adani, among others) and Flender and ZF in gearboxes. Nordex export order book above Rs 200 crore confirmed for the next 12 months; Envision still being onboarded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 33% FY27 growth shape up in H2, and is the 18% EBITDA guidance still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 capacity is sufficient, with 150 crore+ per quarter run-rate and over 300 crore in H2. It expects 17-18% EBITDA margin in H2 and about 100 bp expansion for FY27, with the H1 margin at about 8.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Are elevated production costs expected to normalise, and what is the status of the long-term customer deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs are pass-through with a one-quarter lag, and annual contracts are reset annually. A Nordex export deal of over Rs 200 crore is confirmed, with the US order book fully booked for 12 months; Vestas demand is described as very strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will rising capacity from competitors and the non-wind push pressure the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not concerned about competitors adding capacity, given demand above supply. Non-wind is being scaled back to concentrate on wind, and machine-tool demand is being declined for now.

qa_highlights.question: How long until the company is net profit positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investors should focus on EBITDA and cash profit, which should grow over 50% in FY27. It aims to close the year in the green, with trailing four-quarter profit expected to be positive.

qa_highlights.question: Why is value revenue growth (about 20-23%) lagging volume growth (about 25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is inventory build-up from export shipment delays, which is held at cost and not recognised as revenue. Production growth of 25.8% is not the same as sales volume.

qa_highlights.question: What one-offs were in H1 electricity costs?
qa_highlights.answer: A High Court ruling on solar banking went in MSEDCL's favour, and retrospective charges were levied over two years. Management said about Rs 1.3-1.5 crore of retrospective cost is one-off, and tariff increases are permanent; wind open access is being used to offset them.

qa_highlights.question: Why not expand capacity aggressively given strong demand and the cyclical upturn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution, skilled people and financing at fair valuations are the constraints, not demand. It wants to build demand before capacity and avoid overleveraging. Its target is 25% CAGR, and greenfield is planned for FY29.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (furan, pig iron, CRC) and logistics costs may hold H2 margins below the 17-18% EBITDA target.
Export shipment constraints could keep inventory elevated and push revenue below the 500 crore run-rate, especially with 50% export growth dependent on US shipping.
Only 100-150 bp of inflation pass-through is typical; the one-quarter pricing lag could compress margins if costs rise faster.
Execution risk: the 45,000 tpa plant has ramped only recently (from 30,000 tpa), and machine-shop utilisation is 45-50%.
Greenfield timing (15-18 months build, FY29 target) and funding plans remain unclear; management prefers raising capital at better valuations.
Net profit remains negative in the last two quarters; depreciation and interest weigh on PAT.
Power tariff hikes (Maharashtra over 20%) are a structural cost headwind.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the revenue outlook, but cautious and somewhat defensive on margins and profitability, which management attributes to commodity, logistics and power costs outside its control. Management was evasive on the greenfield timing and capex quantum, and on the exact H2 margin path.
key_quotes: So, as of now, I'm not seeing any, slowdown in, momentum.
So, you should look at a EBITDA value. than a profitability value.
Synergy always built market first, then added the capacity. It's not the other way around.

adds.what: Greenfield foundry expansion (size not given) on top of 45,000 tpa; build 15-18 months, planned for FY29
Further debottlenecking of 10-15% on existing 45,000 tpa capacity being evaluated

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth of 33% (about Rs 500 crore) reaffirmed, backed by 45,000 tpa capacity at ~75% H1 utilisation rising to ~80% for FY27, a Nordex export order book above Rs 200 crore for 12 months and demand above 60,000 tpa; H2 margin recovery to 17-18% rests on pass-through pricing and delayed export shipments, with greenfield deferred to FY29.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 PBDIT margin fell to 8.9% from 15.6% and Q2 to 10.2% from 15.7%; H2 needs 17-18% EBITDA to deliver ~100 bp FY27 expansion, a large step-up that depends on pass-through with a one-quarter lag (only 8-10% of cost rise recovered) and delayed export shipments.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Debottlenecking of 10-15% on the 45,000 tpa base is being evaluated (no date), while greenfield needs 15-18 months and is targeted for FY29; installed capacity was already raised from 30,000 to 45,000 tpa in March 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Utilisation at ~75% in H1 is guided to ~85% in H2 and ~80% for FY27, with demand above 60,000 tpa against 45,000 tpa capacity and a Nordex export order book above Rs 200 crore for 12 months; however, H1 value revenue (+20.2%) lagged production (+25.8%) due to export inventory build.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at ~75-80% with no greenfield amount given; management says greenfield is planned for FY29 but is deferred until current capacity stabilises (about two quarters), and it prefers raising capital at better valuations.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue guidance is held at 33% (~Rs 500 crore) and the H2 margin path is not yet proven; the only upgrade is the revenue potential of the existing 45,000 tpa capacity, raised to Rs 600-650 crore from Rs 550-600 crore, citing inflation pass-through.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 PBDIT margin is 8.9% against a 17-18% H2 EBITDA target, cost inflation (furan up 50%+, logistics roughly 3x, Maharashtra power up over 20%) is ongoing, and export shipments are constrained, so the revenue or margin guide could be cut if the H2 ramp slips.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Machine shop has seven or eight products developed and management expects a good contribution in about 5-6 months, with utilisation at only 45-50% of 20,000 tpa in-house machining capacity.

rows.label: Nordex export order book above Rs 200 crore for 12 months
rows.why: Order book above Rs 200 crore is confirmed for the next 12 months, and the US order book is described as fully booked for 12 months.

rows.label: Quarterly indexation with one-quarter lag on pig iron, CRC and furan
rows.why: Q3 weighted average price increase is about 5%, but pass-through is only about 8-10% of cost increase, implying 100-150 bp margin drag in high-inflation periods.

rows.label: Captive solar and wind open access to offset power tariffs
rows.why: Captive solar and wind open access cover about 60% of electricity needs, and captive solar saves about Rs 7-8/unit versus grid, offsetting a Maharashtra tariff rise of over 20%.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the 33% revenue guide and order book, but cautious and somewhat defensive on margins, blaming commodity, logistics and power costs; analysts pressed on the H2 17-18% EBITDA path, the greenfield timing and capex quantum, which management left vague.
